holidays.name: National Nachos Day
holidays.description: A cheesy celebration of the beloved pile of tortilla chips smothered in melted cheese, jalapeños, beans, and whatever else you can balance on top. Pro tip: the best nachos have toppings in every layer, so no chip is left naked.
holidays.origin: Nachos were invented in 1943 in Piedras Negras, Mexico, by maître d' Ignacio 'Nacho' Anaya, who whipped up a snack for the wives of U.S. soldiers when the kitchen was closed. He topped fried tortilla triangles with cheddar and jalapeños and named them 'Nacho's especiales.'
holidays.funFact: The original nachos had just three ingredients: tortilla chips, cheese, and pickled jalapeños. Ballpark nachos with liquid cheese pump didn't arrive until 1976, at the Texas Rangers stadium.

holidays.name: National Saxophone Day
holidays.description: A day to honor the smooth, sultry, and occasionally squawky instrument that gave us jazz solos, 80s power ballads, and elevator music. Dust off your sax, or at least play some Coltrane while pretending you could.
holidays.origin: The date celebrates the birthday of Adolphe Sax, the Belgian instrument maker who invented the saxophone. He was born on November 6, 1814, in Dinant, Belgium, and patented his creation in 1846.
holidays.funFact: Despite being made of brass, the saxophone is classified as a woodwind because it produces sound with a vibrating reed. Adolphe Sax reportedly survived multiple accidents as a child, including poisoning and a fall from a third-floor window, earning him a reputation as a cursed kid.

holidays.name: International Day for Preventing the Exploitation of the Environment in War and Armed Conflict
holidays.description: A United Nations observance that reminds the world that wars damage forests, farmland, and water supplies, not just people and cities. It is a lesser-known but serious day with a very long name that practically needs its own holiday just to say out loud.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly established it in 2001, designating November 6 each year to highlight the environmental damage caused by armed conflicts and the importance of protecting natural resources.
holidays.funFact: It's likely one of the longest official holiday names on the calendar, clocking in at 17 words, making it a strong contender for the title of 'holiday with the most syllables.'

holidays.name: Marshmallow Fluff Day
holidays.description: An unofficial day for the fluffy, sticky, spoonable white goo that makes sandwiches impossible to eat neatly. Celebrate with a Fluffernutter, the peanut butter and marshmallow creme sandwich beloved in New England.
holidays.origin: Marshmallow creme was popularized in Massachusetts, where Archibald Query began selling his homemade version door to door around 1917. He sold the recipe to H. Allen Durkee and Fred Mower, who turned it into Marshmallow Fluff.
holidays.funFact: The Fluffernutter is so beloved in Massachusetts that in 2006 a state senator proposed a bill to limit how often it could be served in school lunches, prompting another legislator to propose making it the official state sandwich.
